prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1389; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened on a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind. The claimant is represented by a lawyer, and all contact is to go through counsel from here on.

Entry 2: The rear damage to the claimant's vehicle matches the impact as described. No scene photos have been submitted by anyone, and no other report of the collision has been located.

Entry 3: The police record confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. No witnesses have come forward to describe the collision itself.

Entry 4: The driver is named on the policy and is confirmed as the operator. Inspection and prior claim records show no earlier damage to the vehicle, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 5: The claimant reports a wrist fracture, and the injury fits the force expected from a rear impact. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records gathered so far.

Entry 6: Treatment has grown to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits. New body areas were added to the claim several weeks after the collision.

Entry 7: The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation, including the recorded statement and the discussion with counsel. Requested complete prior medical records and noted the treatment pattern for the medical review team.

Entry 8: File remains open pending the medical review and any independent confirmation of the collision itself.
